content: Oxiconazole is an antifungal medication prescribed to treat various skin infections, including athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its use, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist. Oxiconazole is available as a cream or lotion and is applied directly to the skin. It is typically used once daily in the evening or twice daily, in the morning and evening. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. Use the medication exactly as prescribed—do not apply more or less than directed or use it more frequently than instructed. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough to cover the infected area. Wash your hands after applying the medication unless the treatment area is on your hands. Before using oxiconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to oxiconazole or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using oxiconazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed application. Oxiconazole may cause mild side effects, including itching, burning, redness, dry or flaky skin, and tingling. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as pain, swelling, open sores, or a skin rash, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store oxiconazole in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly—consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while using oxiconazole. This medication is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of treatment, contact your doctor. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Oxiconazole is sold under the brand name Oxistat®.
